## What changed, in measured terms

One or two sentences, then the numbers. For a threshold: what it was, what it is now, and
which finding's severity moves as a result - thresholds are the substance of this tool.

## Evidence

Measured output, not a description of it.

- [ ] The four gates are clean locally: `ruff format --check .`, `ruff check .`, `mypy dataset_doctor_audit`, `pytest`
- [ ] Every behaviour change has a test that fails without it, and the test asserts the enum (`AuditStatus`, `FormalImpact`, `Severity`, `EvidenceType`), not the rendered string
- [ ] If a rule changed: `docs/rules/DDNNN-*.md` re-measured in the same commit, and `examples/RESULTS.md` regenerated by `python examples/build.py --audit` rather than edited
- [ ] If the report shape changed: `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped or the field is additive, and `tests/test_docs_contract.py` still passes
- [ ] If a fixture changed: state whether it became stricter or looser, and why (`tests/test_examples.py` is the contract that keeps it honest)

## Why this is the right cut

Link the issue, or the `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` ambiguity-register entry (A-number) this
settles. If it settles none and adds a judgement call, add the register entry in this
commit - an unrecorded decision is the one review comment that always repeats.
